benchmarks: PersonaMem-v2 (own dataset/benchmark, 1,000 personas, 5,000 QA benchmark pairs)
fallos_mitigaciones: Frontier LLMs struggle with implicit personalization overall (37-48% accuracy) and especially with anti-stereotypical (33.0+-5.0%) and dynamic/evolving preferences (35.4+-10.5% vs 40.1+-2.7% for static), and distinguishing others' preferences from the user's own (only 17.5+-11.7%) (S4.1.3). Mitigated partially via GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning (Qwen3-4B reaches 53-56%, beating GPT-5-Chat) and the agentic-memory framework (55% SOTA, 16x fewer tokens), though the ceiling remains far from solved.
cita: Jiang et al. (2025). PersonaMem-v2: Towards Personalized Intelligence via Learning Implicit User Personas and Agentic Memory.
notes: S3.2 agentic memory: Mi=f_theta(Ci,M_{i-1}) sequential chunk-wise update (3 principles: causality/Markovian/capped-size) -> ACTUALIZACION;CONSOLIDACION;WRITE; deterministic fixed-size chunking (trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA); dataset explicitly includes 'user requests to forget prior preferences' in topological conversation order -> OLVIDO. Abstract/S4.2.1: agentic memory achieves 55% accuracy (SOTA) using 16x fewer input tokens (2k memory vs 32k full history) -> COSTO/MEDICION-COSTO. Fig.6 ablation: GRPO trained MCQ-only collapses -13.1pp on open-ended tasks; open-ended-only drops -18.2pp on MCQ and -3.7pp on open-ended itself; mixed 80/20 training is best (Qwen3-4B-GRPO 53.8% MCQ/56.0% open-ended, beats GPT-5-Chat 45.6%/46.2%). S4.1: frontier LLMs only 37-48% on implicit personalization; anti-stereotypical preferences 33.0+-5.0% vs stereotypical 48.9+-5.7% (reliance on population priors); dynamic preferences 35.4+-10.5% vs static 40.1+-2.7% (staleness/update difficulty). No significant gain shortening 128k->32k context -> reasoning not retrieval is the bottleneck (S4.1.2). benchmarks: HumanEval, 3 system-design codebase generation tasks (URL Shortener App et al., from real-world system design interview questions), book-writing task
fallos_mitigaciones: Existing append-only memory methods make errors 'essentially irreversible' and lack mechanisms for 'maintaining syntactic or semantic consistency within the memory store' (S1). Mitigated by L2MAC's precise read/write for entire memory (P2, in-place modification of any file) plus automatic output checking (P3): syntax checkers + self-generated unit tests trigger corrective iteration when mistakes are detected.
cita: Holt et al. (2023). L2MAC: Large Language Model Automatic Computer for Extensive Code Generation.
notes: S3 framework: instruction registry (task-oriented instruction list I, from user task) + file store (final/intermediate code outputs), managed by Control Unit (CU) implementing P1 task-oriented context mgmt / P2 precise read-write / P3 output checking (Fig.1-2). CU deterministically 'declutters context when approaching its limit' (|Ct|<b check, unwind+summarize to Mrs) -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA;PRESUPUESTO. 'Each instruction in turn is executed by a separate LLM agent' sharing the same file store + inheriting summarized progress from prior agents -> explicit 'LLM-based multi-agent system' (abstract) -> MULTIAGENTE=SI, handoff=CONTENIDO. Table2: Code-L2MAC highest Features% across 3 system-design tasks vs GPT4/CodeT/Self-Refine/Reflexion/AutoGPT, fewest syntax errors, most tests passed (10 seeds avg); HumanEval 90.2% Pass@1 SOTA (S6.1). S6.2 insight experiments (P1/P2/P3): Fig.3(a) measures user-specified-feature RETENTION within agents' task instructions/context (read fidelity) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; AutoGPT compresses to 'a mere six-sentence description' losing detail. P3 syntax-checker+unit-test loop triggers corrective actions on memory writes -> FIDELIDAD. F differs from F_screening (WRITE;DOCS-VERSIONADO): added FIDELIDAD, MULTIAGENTE, PROCEDIMENTAL (instruction registry=task plan, plan_estado=SI), RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO.
